front.title: A Centralized Control Plane for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering

abstract.t:
This document specifies a centralized control-plane realization of Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS). The realization uses a logically centralized CATS Path Selector (C-PS) together with ingress and egress CATS-Forwarders. The C-PS receives a service request from an ingress CATS-Forwarder, resolves the requested service to an eligible service contact instance using computing service and network information, and then invokes a path-computation function for the selected destination. The path-computation request contains a resolved headend, endpoint, and network constraints; it does not ask the PCE to discover service instances.
After path computation, the C-PS returns a steering binding to the ingress CATS-Forwarder. The binding identifies the selected destination address, the egress CATS-Forwarder, and a realizable path or policy. The ingress forwarder applies the destination replacement and path encapsulation to the first packet and forwards it. The egress forwarder removes the path encapsulation and delivers the packet to the selected service contact instance. Subsequent packets use the installed flow binding, and reverse traffic uses the corresponding return binding.
